---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
=== bankcache ===
---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
=== bankcache ===
---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

46	// O and the row sum. That much is what the reference does — `build_attn_qsa`

50	// So the mask is also read *before* the key block is, and a block with no
51	// selected cell in any row is skipped whole. The two are the same answer: an
52	// unselected cell contributes nothing to O and nothing to the row sum, so a
53	// block of them contributes nothing, and the skip is bit-identical rather

[← TODO.md](../TODO.md) · [research index](README.md) · [P0](p0-ring-watchdog.md) · [P7](p7-context-depth.md) · [P11](p11-prefill.md) · [P12](p12-prefill-round-two.md)

# P13 — 128k completes, and the key block was twice as wide as it should have been

> **Two results and one refusal.** A 128 000-cell prefill **runs**, for the
> first time in this vertical, because the submit budget had no depth term in
> it. And the attention kernel's key block goes from 32 cells to 16, which is
> **1.46x at 64 000 cells and 1.52x at 128 000** on the block that is 62% of a
> prefill token there — collecting the 1.40x P11-7 priced and then failed to
> collect as a branch. The refusal is the one that looked most promising
> going in: compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is
> **1.00x at every depth**, which is P11-4's finding a third time.

## P13-1: why 128k did not complete, and it was not the marks

TODO.md carried this as "the fill dies at ~115k cells in the P0 timestamp
pathology, reached by depth instead of row count", with "make
`DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional" as the untried route. The
marks were never the problem.

P0 established that a command buffer holding the gfx ring for more than ~2 s
is killed by amdgpu's watchdog, and fitted a cost model to chunk under it:

	322 us a dispatch  +  582 ns a dispatch-row

Every measurement behind that fit was taken **from cell zero**. P11-5 then
measured what a prefill costs at depth — 0.872 ms a token at depth zero and
1.529 at 64 000 cells — and nothing connected the two. So `batchFor(rows)`
went on handing back the same 660 dispatches at 2048 rows whether the cache
was empty or held 128 000 cells, and at 64 000 those 660 already ran for
~1.53 s of the 2 s cliff while the budget believed it was spending 0.86. At
~115 000 the same two chunks cross it.

The fix is the term that was missing. From P12's shipped ladder at 2048 rows,
1207.7 tok/s at depth zero is a 1.696 s pass and 667.7 at 64 000 cells is a
3.067 s one, so the depth term is 1.371 s over `rows * cells`, which is
**10.46 ns each** — `nsPerRowCell = 11` with a little margin, because a submit
that runs long is a ring reset and a dead process where one that runs short is
~40 us of fence wait.

Two things about its shape:

- **Only the attention dispatches carry it.** Every other block of the model
  is flat in depth (P11-5), so charging the term uniformly would make the MoE
  pay for the indexer. The recorder knows each dispatch's owner — that is what
  the attribution is for — so the chunker walks the recorded sequence and cuts
  where the *accumulated* prediction reaches the budget, charging each
  dispatch what its own label costs. At `past = 0` that is exactly P0's answer.
- **It checks itself.** The constants are a fit and a fit is a hypothesis, so
  every submit compares its measured GPU time against what was predicted and
  the ratio scales the next prediction — up at once, down slowly, clamped to
  [0.25, 8]. The recorder already got the GPU time back for the attribution;
  P0's own "what this leaves open" suggested the hook.

Measured, the four chunks of a 2048-row pass at 64 000 cells come in at 1.12,
0.86, 0.97 and 0.57 s against a 2 s cliff, and at 128 000 the pass is five
chunks. `TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth` walks a synthetic 48-layer
pass at every (rows, depth) a 128k context reaches and asserts no chunk is
modelled over budget — and that a one-row pass still chunks only at `maxBatch`,
so **nothing about decode moved**.

### The curve that could not be measured before

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, one
sequence walked forward (`results/p13_depth_base.csv`):

| depth | pp tok/s | vs d0 | tg tok/s | ms a token |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1131.1 | 1.00x | 29.29 | 0.870 |
| 32 000 | 796.7 | 0.70x | 25.84 | 1.205 |
| 64 000 | 661.0 | 0.58x | 24.68 | 1.467 |
| 96 000 | 511.1 | 0.45x | 23.24 | 1.907 |
| **128 000** | **471.7** | **0.42x** | **22.94** | **2.070** |

And where a prefill token goes at 128 000 cells, by label (ms a token):

	attn.attn     0.9107    44.0%      moe.up        0.2770
	attn.select   0.2341    11.3%      moe.down      0.1310
	attn.score    0.0788                dn.qkv        0.0753
	attn.expand   0.0516                hc.cn         0.0581

**Everything that is not the attention block is flat in depth to within 1%**
across the whole sweep — `moe.up` is 0.2828 at depth zero and 0.2770 at
128 000 — which is P11-5's finding carried to twice the depth. The floor is
**0.803 ms a token**, so a prefill at 128 000 cells could not exceed 1245
tok/s at this ubatch even with the attention deleted.

## P13-2: the key block was chosen for the dense regime

P11-7 measured what the QSA selection actually lets the kernel skip, and the
table said what to do:

> the whole remaining headroom is the 1.40x between a 32-cell block and a
> 16-cell one

It then tried to collect it *inside* the kernel — a per-k-tile `kLive[kk]`
flag and a `continue` on it in the QK loop, the row max, the exponential and
the PV loop — measured **1.18x slower**, reverted it, and drew the rule:
**change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it.** What nobody
did was change the granularity, which is a build and not a branch: the rung
`qt1_kt1` did not exist.

The live-pair table at 128 000 cells (`cmd/llm -depth` prints it per depth):

| tile | 16 | 32 | 64 | one row |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | **11.7%** | 17.4% | 25.5% | 7.8% |
| 32 | 16.3 | 23.9 | 34.5 | 7.8 |
| 64 | 22.7 | 32.7 | 45.8 | 7.8 |

A query's cost is `live% x nKV`, so a 16-cell block is 14 976 cells a query
against a 32-cell block's 22 272 — **1.49x**, predicted before anything ran.

Measured, 4 layers (one full-attention layer), `-pp 2048 -ctx 136000`, the
attention block in ms, two passes of the control agreeing to 0.2%:

| rung | depth 0 | 64 000 | 128 000 | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `qt1_kt4` (64-cell block) | 16.9 | 280.1 | 597.4 | 0.63x |
| `qt1_kt2` (32-cell, shipped) | 16.0 | 186.3 | 379.3 | 1.00x |
| **`qt1_kt1` (16-cell)** | 16.3 | **127.2** | **250.1** | **1.46x / 1.52x** |

**The ladder is monotone in the block width at depth and flat at depth zero.**
That is the shape the live-pair table predicts and not the shape L2f's reuse
argument predicts — L2f chose `qt1_kt2` on 512-token prefills from cell zero,
where a 32-cell block is two cooperative-matrix tiles of reuse against one and
the key loop is dense. At depth this kernel is not short of reuse; it is short
of cells it is allowed to skip. So the rung now follows `sparse`:
`AttnKernelFor(sparse)` is `qt1_kt1` where the selection is live and
`qt1_kt2` where it is not, which keeps the dense control arm on the ladder
L2f measured.

`TestAttnGPURungsAgree` is the gate the ladder never had, and the 16-cell rung
is why it is needed: a key block narrower than a mask word is the first shape
in this file where `base` is not a multiple of 32, so the staged bitmask slice
is *half* a word and every `selected` bit moves by `base & 31`. Get that wrong
and the kernel is still a perfectly well-formed attention over the wrong
cells, which every tolerance against llama.cpp passes by being roughly a dense
causal attention. Every rung agrees with the shipped one at **4.6e-5 rms** on
the 4k fixture, where the dense bank the layer reads is itself 5.4e-3 from the
f32 model.

## P13-3: the live-block list, and it is 1.00x

The hypothesis, and it was a good one on paper. `llm_attn_wmma.comp` skips a
key block the selection left empty (P7) but still *walks the axis* to find
out: at 128 000 cells it visits 4000 blocks to do real work in 696 of them,
and each visit stages `BM` words of the bitmask — sixteen separate 64-byte
lines, because a row's mask is `nKV/32` dwords from the next row's — **once
per head**, because the mask is per token and the grid is (query block, head).
Twenty-four heads times 128 query tiles times every block, at 8x line
amplification, is ~6 GB a layer.

So `shaders/llm_attn_blocks.comp` does that OR once for all twenty-four heads,
coalesced, and compacts the live block indices into an ascending list per
query tile with a ballot and a prefix over waves; the attention kernel then
iterates the list instead of the axis. It is **bit-identical** — the list holds
exactly the blocks the skip would not have skipped, in the order the loop
would have met them — and
`TestAttnGPUBlockListDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` asserts that as an equality over
three chunk schedules.

It buys nothing. 48 layers, the same sweep, arm against arm (ms a token):

| | 32 000 | 64 000 | 128 000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `attn.attn` without | 0.2999 | 0.4817 | 0.9107 |
| `attn.attn` with | 0.2979 | 0.4725 | 0.9281 |
| `attn.blocks` | 0.0003 | 0.0005 | 0.0010 |

The compaction itself costs what it was predicted to cost — a thousandth of a
millisecond a token, three orders below what it was meant to save — and the
kernel it feeds does not move. **The mask read was never the cost**: the same
sixteen lines are read by all twenty-four heads of a query tile, the tile's
whole mask is 128 KB at 128 000 cells, and the MALL serves it.

This is **P11-4's finding for the third time**, and at this point it is a
property of the engine rather than an anecdote:

> *Latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do not matter at prefill,
> because prefill has occupancy.* A prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave
> workgroups where a decode step dispatches 24. P11-4 hoisted the block skip
> out of the loop and got 1.00x; P12-4 deleted `hc.cn`'s reduction tree and
> its gamma read and got 1.00x twice; this deletes 83% of the key-block visits
> and gets 1.00x.

The machinery is kept and defaults **off** (`LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` turns it
on) for two reasons: it is the exact converse regime at decode, where the
split kernel walks the same axis with 24 workgroups and no occupancy to hide
behind, and it is the compaction a per-cell gather would be built on.

## What this leaves, and the arithmetic of 900 tok/s at 128k

The target is 900 tok/s at 128 000 cells. After P13-1 and P13-2 the budget at
that depth, at ubatch 2048, is:

	floor (everything flat in depth)   0.803 ms a token
	attn.attn      0.911 -> 0.599      the 16-cell rung
	attn.select    0.234
	attn.score     0.079
	attn.expand    0.052
	                                  = 1.767 ms a token

900 tok/s is **1.111 ms a token**. Two of the four terms above are worth
having and neither is enough on its own:

- **`attn.select` and `attn.expand` together are 0.286**, and they are one
  change. The expansion writes `nKV` floats a token so that the selection can
  radix-select over cells — but all `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one
  block score, so a select over `nKV/ratio` entries with a per-block *weight*
  is the same answer over a quarter of the traffic, and the expansion is then
  not needed at all. It also frees **1.14 GB of arena** at ubatch 2048, which
  is what a wider ubatch wants. P11 priced the traffic at ~2.5x and named the
  risk: the causal boundary, where a block is partly masked and the
  reference's tie fill is a block split. `TestAttnGPUSelectionIsTheCPUs` is
  an exact gate and would catch any drift.
- **The ubatch.** P12 measured 1.13x from 2048 to 4096 rows on the flat floor,
  which is ~0.09 ms a token here. `-llm-batch` already defaults to 4096;
  `-depth` does not.

Both together put 128 000 cells at about **1.39 ms a token, ~720 tok/s**. The
rest has to come from the one thing that has been named since L4b and priced
twice since:

> **The gather.** At 128 000 cells a query tile of sixteen rows selects a
> union of ~4 574 cells and the 16-cell rung reads 14 976 of them — **3.3x**
> more than are wanted, and that is the floor of what a cooperative-matrix
> tile can skip, because the tile is sixteen cells and the selection's runs
> are four. Compacting the union's K and V into a contiguous scratch and
> running a dense attention over it is flat in depth by construction and cuts
> both terms at once: P13's own probe says the kernel at 128 000 cells is
> roughly **half arithmetic and half K/V traffic** (fitting the `qt2_kt2`
> control, which trades 1.46x less K/V a query for 1.37x more work and comes
> out 1.02x *worse*), so 3.3x fewer cells is 3.3x off both halves.
>
> Priced: ~0.25 ms a token at 128 000 including the gather's own traffic,
> against 0.599. With the selection change and the ubatch that is **~1.05 ms
> a token, ~950 tok/s** — the first arrangement of these numbers that reaches
> the target.
>
> The open question is the arena. A per-(query tile, kv head) scratch at 8192
> gathered cells is 2.1 GB, which only fits once the expansion's 1.14 GB is
> freed and the cap is honest; the alternative is chunking the gathered axis
> and folding the partials through P8's combine, which already exists.

Smaller things this sweep priced in passing:

- **`attn.score` is 0.079 ms a token at 128 000** and linear in depth. The
  indexer must score every pooled block, so it is the one term here that is
  the model rather than the implementation.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at ~148k cells**, because the KV
  planes share a buffer with the arenas. 128k fits; 256k needs L6a's
  array-of-buffers, one a layer.
- **Decode at 128 000 cells is 22.94 tok/s**, 0.78x of its depth-zero rate —
  the falloff P7-P10 closed holds to twice the depth they measured it at.

## Reproducing

	go build -o /tmp/pp ./cmd/llm        # once, never `go run` per arm
	export LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
	export LLM_DENSE_BANK=deltanet=q4_k/32,hyper_conn=q5_k/32,lm_head=q5_k/32,full_attn=q5_k/32,qsa_indexer=q5_k/32
	export LLM_MOE_BANK=gate_shexp=q4_k,up_shexp=q4_k,down_shexp=q5_1,down_exps=iq4_nl
	M=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf

	# the headline, ~6 minutes
	/tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,32000,64000,96000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000 -csv results/p13_depth.csv

	# **the fast loop for attention at depth, and it is 40 seconds an arm**
	LLM_ATTN_KERNEL=qt1_kt1 /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

The four-layer prefix is the instrument P13 was built on and it is worth
knowing about: it stages one full-attention layer in ~1 s, fills to 128 000
cells in 15 s, and reports the same `attn.attn` ratios the 48-layer sweep does
at a twelfth of the wall clock. `cmd/llm -attn` cannot replace it — that bench
runs at `past = 0` and so never reaches depth's regime at all.

The gates:

	go test ./llm/ -run TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth        # P13-1
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPURungsAgree                        # P13-2, every rung
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUBlockListDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P13-3, exact
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPU                                  # the block
	go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph

1207.7 tok/s at depth zero is a 1.696 s pass and 667.7 at 64 000 cells is a
3.067 s one, so the depth term is 1.371 s over `rows * cells`, which is
**10.46 ns each** — `nsPerRowCell = 11` with a little margin, because a submit
that runs long is a ring reset and a dead process where one that runs short is
~40 us of fence wait.

Two things about its shape:

- **Only the attention dispatches carry it.** Every other block of the model
  is flat in depth (P11-5), so charging the term uniformly would make the MoE
  pay for the indexer. The recorder knows each dispatch's owner — that is what
  the attribution is for — so the chunker walks the recorded sequence and cuts
  where the *accumulated* prediction reaches the budget, charging each
  dispatch what its own label costs. At `past = 0` that is exactly P0's answer.
- **It checks itself.** The constants are a fit and a fit is a hypothesis, so
  every submit compares its measured GPU time against what was predicted and
  the ratio scales the next prediction — up at once, down slowly, clamped to
  [0.25, 8]. The recorder already got the GPU time back for the attribution;
  P0's own "what this leaves open" suggested the hook.

Measured, the four chunks of a 2048-row pass at 64 000 cells come in at 1.12,
0.86, 0.97 and 0.57 s against a 2 s cliff, and at 128 000 the pass is five
chunks. `TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth` walks a synthetic 48-layer
pass at every (rows, depth) a 128k context reaches and asserts no chunk is
modelled over budget — and that a one-row pass still chunks only at `maxBatch`,
so **nothing about decode moved**.

### The curve that could not be measured before

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, one
sequence walked forward (`results/p13_depth_base.csv`):

| depth | pp tok/s | vs d0 | tg tok/s | ms a token |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1131.1 | 1.00x | 29.29 | 0.870 |
| 32 000 | 796.7 | 0.70x | 25.84 | 1.205 |
| 64 000 | 661.0 | 0.58x | 24.68 | 1.467 |
| 96 000 | 511.1 | 0.45x | 23.24 | 1.907 |
| **128 000** | **471.7** | **0.42x** | **22.94** | **2.070** |

And where a prefill token goes at 128 000 cells, by label (ms a token):

	attn.attn     0.9107    44.0%      moe.up        0.2770
	attn.select   0.2341    11.3%      moe.down      0.1310
	attn.score    0.0788                dn.qkv        0.0753
	attn.expand   0.0516                hc.cn         0.0581

**Everything that is not the attention block is flat in depth to within 1%**
across the whole sweep — `moe.up` is 0.2828 at depth zero and 0.2770 at
128 000 — which is P11-5's finding carried to twice the depth. The floor is
**0.803 ms a token**, so a prefill at 128 000 cells could not exceed 1245
tok/s at this ubatch even with the attention deleted.

## P13-2: the key block was chosen for the dense regime

P11-7 measured what the QSA selection actually lets the kernel skip, and the
table said what to do:

> the whole remaining headroom is the 1.40x between a 32-cell block and a
> 16-cell one

It then tried to collect it *inside* the kernel — a per-k-tile `kLive[kk]`
flag and a `continue` on it in the QK loop, the row max, the exponential and
the PV loop — measured **1.18x slower**, reverted it, and drew the rule:
**change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it.** What nobody
did was change the granularity, which is a build and not a branch: the rung
`qt1_kt1` did not exist.

The live-pair table at 128 000 cells (`cmd/llm -depth` prints it per depth):

| tile | 16 | 32 | 64 | one row |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | **11.7%** | 17.4% | 25.5% | 7.8% |
| 32 | 16.3 | 23.9 | 34.5 | 7.8 |
| 64 | 22.7 | 32.7 | 45.8 | 7.8 |

A query's cost is `live% x nKV`, so a 16-cell block is 14 976 cells a query
against a 32-cell block's 22 272 — **1.49x**, predicted before anything ran.

Measured, 4 layers (one full-attention layer), `-pp 2048 -ctx 136000`, the
attention block in ms, two passes of the control agreeing to 0.2%:

| rung | depth 0 | 64 000 | 128 000 | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `qt1_kt4` (64-cell block) | 16.9 | 280.1 | 597.4 | 0.63x |
| `qt1_kt2` (32-cell, shipped) | 16.0 | 186.3 | 379.3 | 1.00x |
| **`qt1_kt1` (16-cell)** | 16.3 | **127.2** | **250.1** | **1.46x / 1.52x** |

**The ladder is monotone in the block width at depth and flat at depth zero.**
That is the shape the live-pair table predicts and not the shape L2f's reuse
argument predicts — L2f chose `qt1_kt2` on 512-token prefills from cell zero,
where a 32-cell block is two cooperative-matrix tiles of reuse against one and
the key loop is dense. At depth this kernel is not short of reuse; it is short
of cells it is allowed to skip. So the rung now follows `sparse`:
`AttnKernelFor(sparse)` is `qt1_kt1` where the selection is live and
`qt1_kt2` where it is not, which keeps the dense control arm on the ladder
L2f measured.

`TestAttnGPURungsAgree` is the gate the ladder never had, and the 16-cell rung
is why it is needed: a key block narrower than a mask word is the first shape
in this file where `base` is not a multiple of 32, so the staged bitmask slice
is *half* a word and every `selected` bit moves by `base & 31`. Get that wrong
and the kernel is still a perfectly well-formed attention over the wrong
cells, which every tolerance against llama.cpp passes by being roughly a dense
causal attention. Every rung agrees with the shipped one at **4.6e-5 rms** on
the 4k fixture, where the dense bank the layer reads is itself 5.4e-3 from the
f32 model.

## P13-3: the live-block list, and it is 1.00x

The hypothesis, and it was a good one on paper. `llm_attn_wmma.comp` skips a
key block the selection left empty (P7) but still *walks the axis* to find
out: at 128 000 cells it visits 4000 blocks to do real work in 696 of them,
and each visit stages `BM` words of the bitmask — sixteen separate 64-byte
lines, because a row's mask is `nKV/32` dwords from the next row's — **once
per head**, because the mask is per token and the grid is (query block, head).
Twenty-four heads times 128 query tiles times every block, at 8x line
amplification, is ~6 GB a layer.

So `shaders/llm_attn_blocks.comp` does that OR once for all twenty-four heads,
coalesced, and compacts the live block indices into an ascending list per
query tile with a ballot and a prefix over waves; the attention kernel then
iterates the list instead of the axis. It is **bit-identical** — the list holds
exactly the blocks the skip would not have skipped, in the order the loop
would have met them — and
`TestAttnGPUBlockListDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` asserts that as an equality over
three chunk schedules.

It buys nothing. 48 layers, the same sweep, arm against arm (ms a token):

| | 32 000 | 64 000 | 128 000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `attn.attn` without | 0.2999 | 0.4817 | 0.9107 |
| `attn.attn` with | 0.2979 | 0.4725 | 0.9281 |
| `attn.blocks` | 0.0003 | 0.0005 | 0.0010 |

The compaction itself costs what it was predicted to cost — a thousandth of a
millisecond a token, three orders below what it was meant to save — and the
kernel it feeds does not move. **The mask read was never the cost**: the same
sixteen lines are read by all twenty-four heads of a query tile, the tile's
whole mask is 128 KB at 128 000 cells, and the MALL serves it.

This is **P11-4's finding for the third time**, and at this point it is a
property of the engine rather than an anecdote:

> *Latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do not matter at prefill,
> because prefill has occupancy.* A prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave
> workgroups where a decode step dispatches 24. P11-4 hoisted the block skip
> out of the loop and got 1.00x; P12-4 deleted `hc.cn`'s reduction tree and
> its gamma read and got 1.00x twice; this deletes 83% of the key-block visits
> and gets 1.00x.

The machinery is kept and defaults **off** (`LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` turns it
on) for two reasons: it is the exact converse regime at decode, where the
split kernel walks the same axis with 24 workgroups and no occupancy to hide
behind, and it is the compaction a per-cell gather would be built on.

## What this leaves, and the arithmetic of 900 tok/s at 128k

The target is 900 tok/s at 128 000 cells. After P13-1 and P13-2 the budget at
that depth, at ubatch 2048, is:

	floor (everything flat in depth)   0.803 ms a token
	attn.attn      0.911 -> 0.599      the 16-cell rung
	attn.select    0.234
	attn.score     0.079
	attn.expand    0.052
	                                  = 1.767 ms a token

900 tok/s is **1.111 ms a token**. Two of the four terms above are worth
having and neither is enough on its own:

- **`attn.select` and `attn.expand` together are 0.286**, and they are one
  change. The expansion writes `nKV` floats a token so that the selection can
  radix-select over cells — but all `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one
  block score, so a select over `nKV/ratio` entries with a per-block *weight*
  is the same answer over a quarter of the traffic, and the expansion is then
  not needed at all. It also frees **1.14 GB of arena** at ubatch 2048, which
  is what a wider ubatch wants. P11 priced the traffic at ~2.5x and named the
  risk: the causal boundary, where a block is partly masked and the
  reference's tie fill is a block split. `TestAttnGPUSelectionIsTheCPUs` is
  an exact gate and would catch any drift.
- **The ubatch.** P12 measured 1.13x from 2048 to 4096 rows on the flat floor,
  which is ~0.09 ms a token here. `-llm-batch` already defaults to 4096;
  `-depth` does not.

Both together put 128 000 cells at about **1.39 ms a token, ~720 tok/s**. The
rest has to come from the one thing that has been named since L4b and priced
twice since:

> **The gather.** At 128 000 cells a query tile of sixteen rows selects a
> union of ~4 574 cells and the 16-cell rung reads 14 976 of them — **3.3x**
> more than are wanted, and that is the floor of what a cooperative-matrix
> tile can skip, because the tile is sixteen cells and the selection's runs
> are four. Compacting the union's K and V into a contiguous scratch and
> running a dense attention over it is flat in depth by construction and cuts
> both terms at once: P13's own probe says the kernel at 128 000 cells is
> roughly **half arithmetic and half K/V traffic** (fitting the `qt2_kt2`
> control, which trades 1.46x less K/V a query for 1.37x more work and comes
> out 1.02x *worse*), so 3.3x fewer cells is 3.3x off both halves.
>
> Priced: ~0.25 ms a token at 128 000 including the gather's own traffic,
> against 0.599. With the selection change and the ubatch that is **~1.05 ms
> a token, ~950 tok/s** — the first arrangement of these numbers that reaches
> the target.
>
> The open question is the arena. A per-(query tile, kv head) scratch at 8192
> gathered cells is 2.1 GB, which only fits once the expansion's 1.14 GB is
> freed and the cap is honest; the alternative is chunking the gathered axis
> and folding the partials through P8's combine, which already exists.

Smaller things this sweep priced in passing:

- **`attn.score` is 0.079 ms a token at 128 000** and linear in depth. The
  indexer must score every pooled block, so it is the one term here that is
  the model rather than the implementation.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at ~148k cells**, because the KV
  planes share a buffer with the arenas. 128k fits; 256k needs L6a's
  array-of-buffers, one a layer.
- **Decode at 128 000 cells is 22.94 tok/s**, 0.78x of its depth-zero rate —
  the falloff P7-P10 closed holds to twice the depth they measured it at.

## Reproducing

	go build -o /tmp/pp ./cmd/llm        # once, never `go run` per arm
	export LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
	export LLM_DENSE_BANK=deltanet=q4_k/32,hyper_conn=q5_k/32,lm_head=q5_k/32,full_attn=q5_k/32,qsa_indexer=q5_k/32
	export LLM_MOE_BANK=gate_shexp=q4_k,up_shexp=q4_k,down_shexp=q5_1,down_exps=iq4_nl
	M=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf

	# the headline, ~6 minutes
	/tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,32000,64000,96000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000 -csv results/p13_depth.csv

	# **the fast loop for attention at depth, and it is 40 seconds an arm**
	LLM_ATTN_KERNEL=qt1_kt1 /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

The four-layer prefix is the instrument P13 was built on and it is worth
knowing about: it stages one full-attention layer in ~1 s, fills to 128 000
cells in 15 s, and reports the same `attn.attn` ratios the 48-layer sweep does
at a twelfth of the wall clock. `cmd/llm -attn` cannot replace it — that bench
runs at `past = 0` and so never reaches depth's regime at all.

The gates:

	go test ./llm/ -run TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth        # P13-1
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPURungsAgree                        # P13-2, every rung
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUBlockListDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P13-3, exact
	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPU                                  # the block
	go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph

1	<!-- P13. Prompt processing at 128k: the submit budget that was blind to depth,
2	     the key-block width that was chosen for the wrong regime, and the
3	     compaction that is measured inert. Cited from llm/record.go,
4	     llm/gpu_attn.go, shaders/llm_attn_wmma.comp and shaders/llm_attn_blocks.comp. -->
5	
6	[← TODO.md](../TODO.md) · [research index](README.md) · [P0](p0-ring-watchdog.md) · [P7](p7-context-depth.md) · [P11](p11-prefill.md) · [P12](p12-prefill-round-two.md)
7	
8	# P13 — 128k completes, and the key block was twice as wide as it should have been
9	
10	> **Two results and one refusal.** A 128 000-cell prefill **runs**, for the
11	> first time in this vertical, because the submit budget had no depth term in
12	> it — and it runs at **471.7 tok/s**. The attention kernel's key block then
13	> goes from 32 cells to 16, which is **1.61x on `attn.attn` at 128 000 cells**
14	> and takes the prefill there to **563.6 tok/s (1.195x)**: the 1.40x P11-7
15	> priced and failed to collect as a branch, collected as a rung. The refusal
16	> is the one that looked most promising going in — compacting the live key
17	> blocks into a per-query-tile list is **1.00x at every depth**, which is
18	> P11-4's finding a third time.
19	
20	## P13-1: why 128k did not complete, and it was not the marks
21	
22	TODO.md carried this as "the fill dies at ~115k cells in the P0 timestamp
23	pathology, reached by depth instead of row count", with "make
24	`DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional" as the untried route. The
25	marks were never the problem.
26	
27	P0 established that a command buffer holding the gfx ring for more than ~2 s
28	is killed by amdgpu's watchdog, and fitted a cost model to chunk under it:
29	
30		322 us a dispatch  +  582 ns a dispatch-row
31	
32	Every measurement behind that fit was taken **from cell zero**. P11-5 then
33	measured what a prefill costs at depth — 0.872 ms a token at depth zero and
34	1.529 at 64 000 cells — and nothing connected the two. So `batchFor(rows)`
35	went on handing back the same 660 dispatches at 2048 rows whether the cache
36	was empty or held 128 000 cells, and at 64 000 those 660 already ran for
37	~1.53 s of the 2 s cliff while the budget believed it was spending 0.86. At
38	~115 000 the same two chunks cross it.
39	
40	The fix is the term that was missing. From P12's shipped ladder at 2048 rows,
41	1207.7 tok/s at depth zero is a 1.696 s pass and 667.7 at 64 000 cells is a
42	3.067 s one, so the depth term is 1.371 s over `rows * cells`, which is
43	**10.46 ns each** — `nsPerRowCell = 11` with a little margin, because a submit
44	that runs long is a ring reset and a dead process where one that runs short is
45	~40 us of fence wait.
46	
47	Two things about its shape:
48	
49	- **Only the attention dispatches carry it.** Every other block of the model
50	  is flat in depth (P11-5), so charging the term uniformly would make the MoE
51	  pay for the indexer. The recorder knows each dispatch's owner — that is what
52	  the attribution is for — so the chunker walks the recorded sequence and cuts
53	  where the *accumulated* prediction reaches the budget, charging each
54	  dispatch what its own label costs. At `past = 0` that is exactly P0's answer.
55	- **It checks itself.** The constants are a fit and a fit is a hypothesis, so
56	  every submit compares its measured GPU time against what was predicted and
57	  the ratio scales the next prediction — up at once, down slowly, clamped to
58	  [0.25, 8]. The recorder already got the GPU time back for the attribution;
59	  P0's own "what this leaves open" suggested the hook.
60	
61	Measured, the four chunks of a 2048-row pass at 64 000 cells come in at 1.12,
62	0.86, 0.97 and 0.57 s against a 2 s cliff, and at 128 000 the pass is five
63	chunks. `TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth` walks a synthetic 48-layer
64	pass at every (rows, depth) a 128k context reaches and asserts no chunk is
65	modelled over budget — and that a one-row pass still chunks only at `maxBatch`,
66	so **nothing about decode moved**.
67	
68	### The curve that could not be measured before
69	
70	48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, one
71	sequence walked forward (`results/p13_depth_base.csv`):
72	
73	| depth | pp tok/s | vs d0 | tg tok/s | ms a token |
74	|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
75	| 0 | 1131.1 | 1.00x | 29.29 | 0.870 |
76	| 32 000 | 796.7 | 0.70x | 25.84 | 1.205 |
77	| 64 000 | 661.0 | 0.58x | 24.68 | 1.467 |
78	| 96 000 | 511.1 | 0.45x | 23.24 | 1.907 |
79	| **128 000** | **471.7** | **0.42x** | **22.94** | **2.070** |
80	
81	And where a prefill token goes at 128 000 cells, by label (ms a token):
82	
83		attn.attn     0.9107    44.0%      moe.up        0.2770
84		attn.select   0.2341    11.3%      moe.down      0.1310
85		attn.score    0.0788                dn.qkv        0.0753
86		attn.expand   0.0516                hc.cn         0.0581
87	
88	**Everything that is not the attention block is flat in depth to within 1%**
89	across the whole sweep — `moe.up` is 0.2828 at depth zero and 0.2770 at
90	128 000 — which is P11-5's finding carried to twice the depth. The floor is
91	**0.803 ms a token**, so a prefill at 128 000 cells could not exceed 1245
92	tok/s at this ubatch even with the attention deleted.
93	
94	## P13-2: the key block was chosen for the dense regime
95	
96	P11-7 measured what the QSA selection actually lets the kernel skip, and the
97	table said what to do:
98	
99	> the whole remaining headroom is the 1.40x between a 32-cell block and a
100	> 16-cell one
101	
102	It then tried to collect it *inside* the kernel — a per-k-tile `kLive[kk]`
103	flag and a `continue` on it in the QK loop, the row max, the exponential and
104	the PV loop — measured **1.18x slower**, reverted it, and drew the rule:
105	**change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it.** What nobody
106	did was change the granularity, which is a build and not a branch: the rung
107	`qt1_kt1` did not exist.
108	
109	The live-pair table at 128 000 cells (`cmd/llm -depth` prints it per depth):
110	
111	| tile | 16 | 32 | 64 | one row |
112	|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
113	| 16 | **11.7%** | 17.4% | 25.5% | 7.8% |
114	| 32 | 16.3 | 23.9 | 34.5 | 7.8 |
115	| 64 | 22.7 | 32.7 | 45.8 | 7.8 |
116	
117	A query's cost is `live% x nKV`, so a 16-cell block is 14 976 cells a query
118	against a 32-cell block's 22 272 — **1.49x**, predicted before anything ran.

121	attention block in ms, two passes of the control agreeing to 0.2%:

130	token, with every other label as the control:
131	
132	| | 0 | 32 000 | 64 000 | 96 000 | 128 000 |
133	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
134	| `attn.attn` 32-cell | 0.0157 | 0.2999 | 0.4817 | 0.8339 | 0.9107 |
135	| `attn.attn` 16-cell | 0.0167 | **0.2525** | **0.3547** | **0.5198** | **0.5659** |

---
name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P13 (2026-09-22): the rates, the fast 4-layer probe, the rung rule, and the arithmetic of what 900 tok/s at 128k still needs."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**128 000 cells completes as of 2026-09-22 (P13)** and prefills at **563.6
tok/s**. 48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward:

| depth | pp before | pp after | decode |
|------:|----------:|---------:|-------:|
| 0 | 1131.1 | 1129.3 | 29.44 |
| 32 000 | 796.7 | 825.8 | 26.61 |
| 64 000 | 661.0 | **719.6** | 25.01 |
| 96 000 | 511.1 | **607.9** | 23.35 |
| 128 000 | 471.7 | **563.6** | 22.27 |

**Two things changed and one was measured dead.** Write-up
`research/p13-long-context-prefill.md`.

1. **The submit budget had no depth term** — that, not the timestamp marks,
   is why 128k died at ~115k. P0's fit was taken from cell zero, so at 64k a
   2048-row pass already held the ring 1.53 s of the 2 s cliff while the
   budget believed 0.86. The term is 10.46 ns per (row, cell), it is carried
   by the *attention* dispatches only, and the chunker now walks the recorded
   sequence charging each dispatch its own label and rescales against the last
   submit's measured time.
2. **The attention key block should be 16 cells at depth, not 32.** New rung
   `qt1_kt1`; `attn.attn` 0.9107 → 0.5659 ms a token at 128k (**1.61x**),
   and 1.19x / 1.36x / 1.60x at 32k / 64k / 96k. It is **prefill's rung
   only** — with it at decode too, 128k decode went 22.94 → 22.27, because a
   decode step costs one wave's serial walk and halving the block doubles it.
3. **Compacting the live key blocks into a list is 1.00x at every depth.**
   It deletes 83% of the axis walk and costs 0.001 ms a token. Off by default
   (`LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1`), bit-identical. This is P11-4's finding a third
   time — see [[prefill-rates]].

**The fast loop, and it is 40 seconds an arm**: `-depth ... -layers 4`. One
full-attention layer, stages in ~1 s, fills to 128 000 in 15 s, and reproduces
the 48-layer `attn.attn` ratios. `cmd/llm -attn` cannot replace it — that
bench runs at `past = 0`. Two passes of a control agree to 0.2%.

    LLM_ATTN_KERNEL=qt1_kt1 /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 \
        -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

**What 900 tok/s at 128k still needs.** Budget at 128k, ubatch 2048 (ms a
token): floor 0.803 (everything not attention is flat in depth to 1%),
`attn.attn` 0.566, `attn.select` 0.233, `attn.score` 0.078, `attn.expand`
0.051 = 1.731. 900 tok/s is 1.111. The selection change (select over
`nKV/ratio` block scores, delete the expansion, frees 1.14 GB of arena) plus
ubatch 4096 reach **~700**. **Only the per-cell gather reaches 900**: a
16-row tile's union is ~4574 selected cells and the 16-cell rung reads 14 976,
so 3.3x, priced at ~0.20 ms a token → ~940 tok/s. P13's probe says
`attn.attn` at 128k is ~half arithmetic and ~half K/V traffic (the `qt2_kt2`
control: 1.46x less K/V a query for 1.37x more work is 1.02x *worse*), so
fewer cells is the only thing that cuts both.

**`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at ~148k cells** — the KV planes
share a buffer with the arenas. Past that wants one buffer a layer.

**Gates**: `TestChunkEndIsUnderTheWatchdogAtDepth`, `TestAttnGPURungsAgree`
(every rung against the shipped one, 4.6e-5 rms),
`TestAttnGPUBlockListDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` (exact). See
[[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]], [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

content.content:
>
> The open question is the arena. A per-(query tile, kv head) scratch at 8192
> gathered cells is 2.1 GB, which only fits once the expansion's 1.14 GB is
> freed and the cap is honest; the alternative is chunking the gathered axis
> and folding the partials through P8's combine, which already exists.

Smaller things this sweep priced in passing:

- **`attn.score` is 0.079 ms a token at 128 000** and linear in depth. The
  indexer must score every pooled block, so it is the one term here that is
  the model rather than the implementation.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at ~148k cells**, because the KV
  planes share a buffer with the arenas. 128k fits; 256k needs L6a's
  array-of-buffers, one a layer.
- **Decode at 128 000 cells is 22.94 tok/s**, 0.78x of its depth-zero rate —
  the falloff P7-P10 closed holds to twice the depth they measured it at.
- **The narrow rung is prefill's and not decode's**, and the sweep that tried
  it on both is why: with `qt1_kt1` everywhere, decode at 128 000 went
  **22.94 -> 22.27 tok/s** while prefill went 471.7 -> 563.6. That is P8's
  finding in the other direction — a decode step is 24 single-wave workgroups
  that all fit at once, so it costs one wave's *serial walk*, and halving the
  key block doubles the walk. `AttnKernelFor` takes the rung from the row
  count at the same `attnSplitMaxRows` boundary the split already turns on.

## Reproducing

	go build -o /tmp/pp ./cmd/llm        # once, never `go run` per arm
	export LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
	export LLM_DENSE_BANK=deltanet=q4_k/32,hyper_conn=q5_k/32,lm_head=q5_k/32,full_attn=q5_k/32,qsa_indexer=q5_k/32

content.content:
106:| [P12](p12-prefill-round-two.md) | **Prefill round two: two bit-exact kernel changes, and four of P11's own leads measured away.** Prefill is **1.012-1.025x on both axes** — 1191.2 → **1207.7 tok/s** at 2048 rows, 1370.5 → **1403.9** at 8192 (**3.59x** llama.cpp), and 651.3 → **667.7** at 64 000 cells — with the two base passes agreeing to 1370.5/1370.5 and 651.3/651.2. Two changes hold. **The attention kernel's row max ran on sixteen lanes of sixty-four**: `for (i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE)` with BM 16 and WAVE 64, KTIL times a block, two barriers and a store around each pass, each active lane then walking TILE cells serially with a `selected()` bit test. The whole key block is now staged at once (`stage` holds QT\*KTIL tiles, 2 KB of LDS) and RCL = WAVE/BM lanes share a row, folded by a **clustered subgroup max** — **bit-identical**, because a max has no rounding and the cells scanned are the same ones in the same order, and the wave is converged where the op is issued. **1.16x on the kernel at 512 tokens** and **+1.6-1.8% of a prefill token from 8000 cells on**. And **a K-quant block's header is one sixteen-byte load, not four dwords**: Q4_K/Q5_K open every block with `d`, `dmin` and twelve packed scale bytes, so at BK 32 a lane was issuing eight scalar loads a K-step against the nibbles' four `uvec4`s — L5b-7's rule for the third time. Every block of both formats is 16-byte aligned (region, row and block all multiples of 16) and `MoEGPU.build` now says so rather than trusting it; with the nibble extracted in two ops instead of four it is **`moe.up` 12 118 → 11 755 µs at 2048 tokens (1.031x)** with **`moe.down` (IQ4_NL, untouched) flat as the control**. **And four refusals, which close most of P11's open list.** **Both of `hc.cn`'s named suspects cost nothing**: deleting the 256-way reduction tree outright measures **5331.5 µs against 5325.8** — the eight barriers four times a token are **free**, so the non-bit-exact rewrite queued behind them would have bought zero — and replacing the per-token `gamma` read with a constant measures **5332.9**, because it is the same 40 KB every token and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy bandwidth is now unexplained *and* out of hypotheses. **The block skip hoisted out of the loop is 1.00x at every depth**: at 64k a query tile walks ~2000 blocks and skips ~1480, each paying a **dependent** global read, and a cost model where a dead block is ~20% of a live one reproduces `attn.attn`'s 9.8-against-16.0 TFLOP/s exactly — so the whole key range was voted on up front in one coalesced pass with a subgroup ballot, no atomics and no per-block barrier, and it bought **nothing**. The reason is the **exact converse of P8**: a decode step dispatches 24 single-wave workgroups and nothing hides a serial walk, but a 2048-token prefill dispatches **3072**, so that latency is already covered — *latency that matters at decode does not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy*. It is still live for decode, where it was deliberately never built. **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%**, not the rest of the gap. **The MoE's per-element affine is a floor**: gutting the whole scale path is 1.21x at 2048 tokens, P12-2 takes the loads and integer ops out of that, and what remains — an int→float convert, an FMA and an f16 convert on every weight — has no bit-exact cheaper form, since packed fp16 costs thirteen bits of mantissa and `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds the wrong way. **The ubatch remains the largest number on the board**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x and the curve has not flattened, which is a memory budget rather than a kernel. |
107:| [P11](p11-prefill.md) | **Prompt processing: the ubatch was the largest number in the file and the cheapest, and the MoE's row padding is not a cost at all.** `cmd/serve` prefilled in **512-token chunks** because that is llama.cpp's best ubatch and what every number in this vertical is quoted against — and 512 is the **worst rung this graph has**. llama.cpp plateaus at its ubatch; this one does not, because the MoE's arithmetic intensity is the **routing's**: at 512 tokens 274 of 512 experts are unpacked whole to serve 5120 rows, and the schedule pads those out to 11 904. `-llm-batch` is now **2048** — 1.12 GB of arenas for **1.64x** (667.4 → 1093.3 tok/s at 48 layers and ctx 4096; **667 → 1053 through HTTP** on a 4128-token prompt), where the 1.49 GB to 4096 buys 13% more. The compaction itself costs what it was predicted to cost — a thousandth of a
millisecond a token, three orders below what it was meant to save — and the
kernel it feeds does not move. **The mask read was never the cost**: the same
sixteen lines are read by all twenty-four heads of a query tile, the tile's
whole mask is 128 KB at 128 000 cells, and the MALL serves it.

This is **P11-4's finding for the third time**, and at this point it is a
property of the engine rather than an anecdote:

> *Latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do not matter at prefill,
> because prefill has occupancy.* A prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave
> workgroups where a decode step dispatches 24. P11-4 hoisted the block skip
> out of the loop and got 1.00x; P12-4 deleted `hc.cn`'s reduction tree and
> its gamma read and got 1.00x twice; this deletes 83% of the key-block visits
> and gets 1.00x.

And it does not become worth anything at the narrow rung either, where there
are twice as many dead blocks to skip: at 4 layers and 128 000 cells the
attention block is **238.6 ms without the list and 251.2 with it**, because
the compaction's own scan doubles with the block count while what it buys
stays zero.

The machinery is kept and defaults **off** (`LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` turns it
on) for two reasons: it is the exact converse regime at decode, where the
split kernel walks the same axis with 24 workgroups and no occupancy to hide
behind, and it is the compaction a per-cell gather would be built on.

content.text:
Done. Here's where long-context prefill stands.

## What I found and changed

**1. 128k prefill didn't complete — and the diagnosis in `TODO.md` was wrong.**

It wasn't the timestamp marks. P0's submit budget (`322 µs/dispatch + 582 ns/dispatch-row`) was fitted entirely from cell zero, so it handed back the same 660 dispatches at 2048 rows whether the cache was empty or held 128k cells. At 64k those 660 already held the ring for ~1.53 s of amdgpu's 2 s watchdog while the budget believed it was spending 0.86; at ~115k they cross it.

The missing term is **10.46 ns per (row, cell)**, read straight off P12's own ladder, and only the attention dispatches carry it. The chunker now walks the recorded sequence and cuts where accumulated predicted cost hits the budget, and rescales against what the last submit measured — **upwards only** (a decode step is predicted at ~330 ms where it runs in ~36, so a scale that learned from decode would hand the next prefill 4× its budget; `TestObserveNeverLoosensTheBudget` is that line).

**128k now runs: 471.7 tok/s.**

**2. The attention key block was twice as wide as it should be at depth.** L2f chose `qt1_kt2` on 512-token prefills from cell zero, where a 32-cell block is two coopmat tiles of reuse against one. At depth the cost is the *union* of 16 adjacent queries' selections at the block's width — 11.7% of the axis at 16 cells vs 17.4% at 32. The new `qt1_kt1` rung is **1.61× on `attn.attn` at 128k** (0.9107 → 0.5659 ms/token), with `attn.select`/`score`/`expand` identical to three decimals as the control:

| depth | before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1131.1 | 1129.3 |
| 32 000 | 796.7 | 825.8 |
| 64 000 | 661.0 | **719.6** |
| 96 000 | 511.1 | **607.9** |
| **128 000** | **471.7** | **563.6** |

Two passes agree to 0.05–0.2%. It's prefill's rung only — on decode it went the other way (22.94 → 22.27), since a decode step costs one wave's serial walk and halving the block doubles it.

**3. One refusal.** I built the live-block compaction (`llm_attn_blocks.comp`, bit-identical, gated as an equality) that deletes 83% of the axis walk. It is **1.00× at every depth**, and 1.05× *against* at the narrow rung. The mask read was never the cost — the MALL serves it. That's P11-4's finding a third time. It ships behind `LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` because decode and a future gather both want it.

## On 900 tok/s at 128k — not reached, and here is the arithmetic

Budget at 128k, ubatch 2048 (ms/token): floor **0.803** (everything not attention is flat in depth to 1%), `attn.attn` **0.566**, `attn.select` **0.233**, `attn.score` 0.078, `attn.expand` 0.051 → 1.731. The target is 1.111.

- Block-granular selection (select over `nKV/ratio` block scores, delete the expansion; also frees 1.14 GB of arena) − 0.22
- ubatch 4096 − 0.09 → **~700 tok/s**
- **Only the per-cell gather reaches 900.** A 16-row tile's union is ~4 574 selected cells and the 16-cell rung reads 14 976 — 3.3×, and that's the floor of what a coopmat tile can skip. Priced at ~0.20 ms/token → **~940 tok/s**. P13's probe (the `qt2_kt2` control: 1.46× less K/V per query for 1.37× more work is 1.02× *worse*) says `attn.attn` at 128k is ~half arithmetic, ~half K/V traffic, so fewer cells is the only thing that cuts both.

So 900 is reachable but needs the gather; P13 took it from needing 4.9× to needing 2.8×.

Write-up in `research/p13-long-context-prefill.md`, CSVs in `results/p13_*`, `TODO.md` updated. `go test ./llm/` passes (176 s), including `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit`. One practical note: the fast loop for this is `-depth ... -layers 4` — 40 seconds an arm, and it reproduces the 48-layer ratios.
